newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa appeals for funds for AIDS victims.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa appeals for funds for AIDS victims.

text.p: Mother Teresa appealed to U.S. and Indian businessmen on Sunday for funds to open centres dedicated to caring for people suffering from AIDS all over the world.

"I need more funds for setting up caring centres for the AIDS victims," the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner said after receiving an award from the Indo-American Society, a group of volunteers and businessmen from both countries.
"They too are the children of God and they need more care," she said. "I will make all of you work for that."
The society gave the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun a 100,000-rupee ($2,800) award for promoting a spirit of service and sacrifice all over the world.
The Calcutta-based Missionaries of Charity order that Mother Teresa founded in 1948 already runs at least five homes for people suffering from Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.

Last year, the Missionaries of Charity fed more than half a million people in some 111 countries. It teaches some 20,000 children in its schools and treats 90,000 lepers in its clinics. It also runs orphanages and homes for the dying.
The religious order guides hundreds of volunteers who queue up to face lives of hardship, apart from some 4,500 nuns around the world. ($ = 35.78 Indian Rupees)
